Planning key `CC-12`. Phase V1. Milestone `M3`. Type delivery.

## Outcome

The migration/operator tooling supports the newer 2,131-document generation and the newer JSON-style generation through one validated results-package contract, retaining original v5 compatibility. Import/adapter work is already merged on dev; inspect current implementation and exact-revision evidence before adding code. Do not treat a merged PR or unit tests alone as acceptance.

## Dependencies

[GRS-21](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-21/verify-complete-v5-parity-and-local-release-readiness>)

## Write scope

* `src/lib/case-package/v5/newer-workspace.ts`
* `src/lib/case-package/v5/json-workspace.ts`
* Related format detection/mapping under `src/lib/case-package/v5/**`, only after confirming current ownership
* `tests/case-package/**` and existing compatibility acceptance probes
* `docs/compatibility.md`

## Acceptance

- [ ] Identify the source format explicitly and preserve all 2,131 chronology rows, 24 DATA keys and two auxiliary top-level datasets in the observed export. Confirm counts from the source before coding.
- [ ] Handle changed shapes such as storyline records and numeric/string row positions through the format adapter, not scattered UI conditionals.
- [ ] Document extra dataset presentation or an explicit unsupported state for every new dataset. Preserve attachment sources and disclose the 4,000-character text cap.
- [ ] Re-run all v5 gates after adding compatibility. Ref collisions between versions never silently attach old notes to a different original.
- [ ] Recheck BA-04, BA-05, BA-07, BA-09 and BA-11 on the newer export. Date basis, classification/identity uncertainty, direct-versus-parent originals and email-subset coverage must be explicit wherever those datasets are presented. An unsupported view/dataset is reported as unsupported, not as a completed feature. Full metadata re-extraction and expanded OCR remain deferred.
- [ ] Verify the JSON-style export generation against its own source inventory and counts, with explicit detection rather than ad hoc UI checks.
- [ ] Preserve unrecognized sections privately and expose repair/coverage diagnostics. Unsupported or invalid required sections prevent publication; opaque residual retention with a warning is not complete presentation. Optional unsupported information must not silently disappear.

## Verification

Report PASS, HOLD or FAIL at the exact reviewed revision. Include commands, exit codes and artifact paths. A skipped check is not a pass. Read the local delivery plan and orchestration protocol before dispatch.

## Boundaries

Keep RAWS and current production read-only. Do not commit case documents, extracted text or secrets. No Cursor agents; every Opus agent uses high effort. Only the coordinator updates Linear. No deployment, production publication or external messages under this issue without the appropriate execution authority.

items.outcome: See the synchronized Linear description.
items.linearDescription:
## Destination

A user-approved, agent-navigable plan for ClearCase 0.1 alpha: convert the client-alignment POC into an intuitive hosted case application, initially for one or two clients with a separate instance and subdomain each. Align scope, stack, UX, ADRs, Linear milestones, delivery dependencies and acceptance gates before implementation starts.

## Notes

This is the canonical planning map and retains the existing realignment gate. No V2 implementation begins until this issue is Done. Done requires the user's approval of the written scope, architecture, milestones and ordered implementation tickets, with blocked issues reconciled.

Use grill-with-docs, grilling and domain-modeling for decision sessions; wayfinder for map maintenance. Resolve at most one decision ticket per session. Claim a child by assigning it to the person driving the decision before work. Query open, unassigned children whose native blockers are closed for the frontier. Use only wayfinder labels on map and decision children. Record answers in resolution comments and index closed children here. Keep implementation tickets separate.

User direction is recorded in this issue's interview comments, dated 14 October. Retain production capabilities, conduct a software and dependency audit, improve information grouping and in-app viewing, and implement manual queue/download/processing/upload/private-preview/approval/publication first. Checks and review throughout, plus final gates. Fable and swarm are requested for later execution; reconcile the older operating rules before dispatch.

Original case archives and production are read-only. Real case data, extracted text, private screenshots and credentials stay out of Git and external agent/test services. No production changes, deployment or main merge is authorized by this planning map.

Existing POC acceptance and unfinished demo/compatibility work are inputs, not assumed hosted acceptance. Older Cloudflare, local-product and automation assumptions are subject to decisions here.

## Decisions so far

* [Define client instances, membership and case permissions](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-85/define-client-instances-membership-and-case-permissions>): isolated client instances, Clerk authentication, assigned viewer/editor case access, and distinct Global Admin, firm-admin and audited operator authority. The resolution comment holds the full decision.
* [Define the manual processing queue and results handoff](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-87/define-the-manual-processing-queue-and-results-handoff>): mostly FIFO claimed jobs, corrected submissions rejoin last, and one candidate-import contract for manual processing and later automation. SLA measurement is deferred to release evidence.
* [Assess D1 and R2 performance and overhead for the alpha workload](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-95/assess-d1-and-r2-performance-and-overhead-for-the-alpha-workload>): D1/R2 remains a reasonable candidate; local CPU evidence does not prove hosted performance. The ticket links the corrected research and required hosted probes.
* [Define private preview, approval and client publication](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-88/define-private-preview-approval-and-client-publication>): editable, audited candidates require exact-version sign-off; alpha permits preparer approval, recovery preserves user work, and later processing flags correction conflicts. Review topology awaits the design gate.
* [Define an intuitive case workspace and information hierarchy](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-89/define-an-intuitive-case-workspace-and-information-hierarchy>): retain the current app navigation as the planning baseline; the user and UX lead will explore later designs in Figma. The prototypes remain research, and the resolution retains the settled Notes and mobile requirements.
* [Assess browser viewers and manual previews for alpha file types](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-96/assess-browser-viewers-and-manual-previews-for-alpha-file-types>): manual derived previews make the minimum families and conditional media/ZIP browsing feasible in principle; rendition fidelity and fail-closed range integrity still require proof. The ticket links the corrected research.
* [Define in-app file viewing and original integrity](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-90/define-in-app-file-viewing-and-original-integrity>): every accepted file is viewable in-app, original/processed references remain traceable, failed previews hold publication, and complete exports include originals and published previews. A dedicated component evaluation and integrated viewer gate are planned.
* [Assess Outlook drafts and user-controlled case-email import](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-98/assess-outlook-drafts-and-user-controlled-case-email-import>): Graph drafts and selected-message import are feasible candidates with mailbox-wide consent and durable-copy constraints; the research informs the later live-integration pass, with synthetic proofs still unrun.
* [Define alpha behavior for every production integration](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-91/define-alpha-behavior-for-every-production-integration>): provider-neutral email files and app-side drafts in alpha, manual KYC and existing case costs, scoped audit access, explicit privilege handling and protected bundle history. Live mailbox connections are later; the ticket resolution holds the full decision.
* [Reconcile POC, demo and newer-export work with the hosted plan](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-92/reconcile-poc-demo-and-newer-export-work-with-the-hosted-plan>): preserve reviewed work and v5 contracts, support newer/JSON exports, hold unsupported required sections, and use controlled E2E preservation tests; no live-client migration is needed. Standalone Markdown authoring is later.
* [Audit hosted software choices and Clerk–Workers integration](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-100/audit-hosted-software-choices-and-clerk-workers-integration>): dated dependency/advisory inventory, Clerk integration and residency constraints, local Workers testing and Void comparison are published. Adoption and all runtime proofs remain with the stack decision.
* [Assess a local agent test platform on PC1 and PC2](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-101/assess-a-local-agent-test-platform-on-pc1-and-pc2>): local Workers tooling and both PCs’ read-only capacity are assessed; PC2 is the recommended first pool candidate, while the delivery decision holds roles, isolation proofs and measured concurrency. No platform is installed.
* [Assess cf and Void for the alpha agent tooling jobs](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-102/assess-cf-and-void-for-the-alpha-agent-tooling-jobs>): released source supports a Void/Kit 3 prebuilt route and cf resource/automation jobs; native D1, credential separation and same-account client boundaries have explicit unrun proofs. Research is published, without tool adoption or cloud execution.
* [Choose the hosted stack and software audit criteria](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-86/choose-the-hosted-stack-and-software-audit-criteria>): SvelteKit 3/Workers with Bun app builds and supported Node tooling; D1/R2, separate client/staff Clerk apps and invite-only access; MFA initially off. Void/cf are preferred proof candidates with Wrangler fallback. The resolution holds the accepted constraints and required proofs.
* [Research Cloudflare-first transactional alpha notifications](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-103/research-cloudflare-first-transactional-alpha-notifications>): native email is a feasible candidate with separate free/Paid recipient paths, delivery/retry constraints and unrun proofs. Research is published; provider and notification-failure choices remain with acceptance planning.
* [Define alpha acceptance, rollout and recovery](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-93/define-alpha-acceptance-rollout-and-recovery>): accepted outcome/evidence checklist, practical rollout guidance, soft recovery timing, data-recovery/deletion policy, initial notifications and user-owned release/incident/spend decisions. Later SLA/reliability refinement stays explicit; hosted proofs remain unrun.
* [Stress-test the complete hosted-alpha plan with final workflow scenarios](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-136/stress-test-the-complete-hosted-alpha-plan-with-final-workflow>): early hosted PDF workflow before broad migration, explicit pending-preview and supplement rules, usable unpublished cases, and prompt optimization after stabilization.

## Not yet specified

No additional unticketed planning questions are currently identified. Surface any further questions as the remaining delivery operating plan is worked.

## Out of scope

Executing the hosted build in this charting session; maintaining a separately shipped local product as an alpha requirement. Automated processing is later work, after the manual workflow is proven. Main merges and deployment remain under the user's control.

[Plan live Outlook and Gmail integrations after alpha](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-99/plan-live-outlook-and-gmail-integrations-after-alpha>) preserves the explicitly deferred live mailbox connections, provider-side draft creation and syncing. Alpha handles exported provider-neutral email files; this later work does not block alpha.

[Round-trip one manually authored analysis through Markdown](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-23/round-trip-one-manually-authored-analysis-through-markdown>) is preserved in M7 after alpha. Validated package upload and editable private preview cover alpha; Markdown no longer blocks hosted delivery. There are no current live clients requiring production migration or cutover; controlled preservation/recovery E2E remains in scope.

## Outcome

A prompt change to the V2 processing prompt pack gets three separate verdicts from one command: does it still resolve functionally the same (Function), is the content better or worse (Content), and has rigour been lost (Rigour).

V2 rewrites the pack (`RAWS/ClearCase Prompts.zip`, which today produces a single-file HTML) so that the model emits data only. For each section it writes one JSONL file whose records have a stable `id`, an `order` and `refs[]`. A new adapter compiles those files into the existing `v5.*@1` datasets of a results package. This issue builds the harness that measures any prompt change, plus one pilot section (the risk matrix) that goes through it end to end. ADR 0006 (`docs/adr/0006-v2-prompt-pack-data-contract-and-evals.md`, in review) records the decisions.

## Scope

* `bun run --bun evals` CLI, with results under the ignored `.local/evals/`:
  * `check`: free code checks, runs in seconds.
  * `run <section> --k N --live|--replay --budget USD`.
  * `compare vN vM <section>`.
  * `calibrate <section> --labels FILE`.
  * `show <run> --failures`.
* Three layers of checks:
  * L0 compares sections that code generates to golden files. These are the document index and derived data: prescription, recon, counts, and copied titles and dates.
  * L1 reuses the `validate` code checks (shape, counts, refs, unresolved citations, bare mentions, links, dates) and adds new ones:
    * derived fields agree with the chronology;
    * enums, and length bounds;
    * `id` and `order` present, and `id` continuity between runs;
    * authorities appear on an allow-list;
    * the prescription interruption date is cited and within range.
  * L2 is model-graded: key-fact coverage, citation support, rigour counts, pairwise comparison. It runs only in the eval loop, with k samples, a cost cap, and a record and replay cache.
  * L0 and L1 run in `gate`. L2 never runs in `gate` or CI.
* Model calls use `output_config.format` with a JSON schema. The harness checks refs in code. It sets effort explicitly on every call, because Opus 5.5 defaults to medium. It sends no sampling parameters, because they return 400 on the 5.5 models.
* Gold sets:
  * Tier 1 is a synthetic case with planted facts, built by extending `scripts/fixtures/v5fixture/`. It runs in CI.
  * Tier 2 uses the authored datasets of the v5 sample as the baseline on the real case. It runs locally only.
  * Human-labelled sets come later. Until then, judge scores are advisory and never pass or fail a change.
* Each section has one prompt template, one JSON schema and one gold checklist.

## Out of scope

Rewriting the prompts beyond the one pilot section. OCR, which is a separate research item. The `@2` schemas. Hosted processing.

## Blockers

None are hard. Related: [GRS-22](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-22/import-and-verify-the-newer-2131-document-export>), [GRS-23](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-23/round-trip-one-manually-authored-analysis-through-markdown>), [GRS-33](<https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-33/design-pi-durable-processing-against-the-proven-manual-contract>).

- [ ] One L2 run at k=5 has its cost recorded. A `--replay` of that run costs nothing.
- [ ] `compare` prints Function, Content and Rigour verdicts with paired confidence intervals.
- [ ] No case text, names or amounts appear in Git, fixtures, or any JSON schema sent to the API. A leak scan passes.
- [ ] No L2 code path is reachable from `gate` or CI. A test shows it.

## Verification

Report PASS or FAIL at an exact SHA. `bun run --bun gate` must be green at that SHA. Report the spend of the L2 run in USD, and the paths of the recorded run and its replay under `.local/evals/`.

## Forbidden

Case text, names or amounts in Git, fixtures or JSON schemas. L2 in `gate` or CI. Codex, Cursor, and effort `max`. Writes to `RAWS/` or production.

items.linearDescription:
Planning key `HA-ci-verdict`. From the read-only CI review of 17 October 2026 (`clearcase/.orchestration/reports/CI-REVIEW-20261017/report.md`). Infrastructure work on the CI runner, not hosted-app work; it may run before the hosted plan gate.

## Why

CI is already fast (median job 57 s, median queue 4 s over the last 23 runs, no infrastructure failures). The gap is that an agent cannot learn whether a SHA passed when GitHub is down, and the runner's own idle check asks the GitHub API and fails closed in that case. Recent GitHub outages made this matter.

## What to build

1. `scripts/ci/pc1-vm verify REV`: bundle the revision, confirm in the guest that no job is running without asking GitHub (`pgrep -u runner Runner.Worker`), stop the runner service, run the job's exact commands under `scripts/agent-tools/receipt`, run the summary, write the result to the store below, restart the runner, and print `PASS <sha>` or `FAIL <sha>` plus the receipt path. Exit 0 only on PASS.
2. A receipt store in the guest keyed by commit: `~runner/ci-results/<sha>-<run>-<attempt>/`, written by every GitHub-dispatched job as one extra workflow step (recording both `GITHUB_SHA` and `PR_HEAD_SHA`, since a PR run tests the merge commit) and by `verify`. The guest cannot reach pc1 by design, so the store lives in the guest and is read over the existing management SSH; do not open a guest-to-host path.
3. `scripts/ci/pc1-vm verdict SHA`: read the store and print the verdict and receipt path for a SHA GitHub or `verify` already ran, or `UNKNOWN`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With GitHub unreachable (simulate by pointing `GH_HOST` at a dead name), `verify` still produces a verdict for a fresh bundle, and `verdict` still answers for a SHA that ran earlier.
- [ ] `verify` refuses to start while a job is running and never leaves the runner service stopped; a failed run restarts it.
- [ ] A `verify` verdict names what it proves (that bundle's SHA passed `check` and `test` in the CI VM environment) and does not claim a GitHub check status or satisfy branch protection or the external reviewer.
- [ ] Receipts carry no tokens or secrets; the store survives a guest reboot and is documented as lost on `destroy`.
- [ ] `docs/ci-runner.md` documents both commands, the store layout and the trust model (any job can write the store; it is as trusted as a push).

## Reserved write scope

* scripts/ci/pc1-vm
* scripts/ci/guest-provision.sh (store directory only)
* .github/workflows/ci.yml (one receipt-store step)
* docs/ci-runner.md

items.linearDescription:
Planning key `HA-ci-second-guest`. From the read-only CI review of 17 October 2026 (`clearcase/.orchestration/reports/CI-REVIEW-20261017/report.md`). Optional: it buys redundancy and removes the 40 to 75 s queue waits when a PR run and a dev merge overlap. It does not shorten a job. Do it after the CI verdict ticket, and only after pc1's headroom is measured.

## What to build

Make `scripts/ci/vm-host.sh` and `scripts/ci/pc1-vm` instance-aware so a second guest can be created without touching the first: a template unit `clearcase-ci-vm@N`, a separate `/var/lib/clearcase-ci-N`, its own SSH forward address and port in `IPAddressAllow=` and the nft reply rule, its own nft table (today one instance's `ExecStopPost` would delete a shared table), its own QMP socket, hostname, `HostKeyAlias` and runner name, and the busy check per runner name. Instance 1 keeps today's paths. Prefer several guests over several runners in one guest: runners in one guest would share the Chrome cache that `install-chrome.sh` deletes, `~/.bun`, `/dev/shm` and one network namespace for the tests' local servers. `ci.yml` needs no change; every runner carries the `clearcase-pc1` label and the per-ref concurrency group already lets different PRs run at once.

## Before sizing

Measure RAM per job with the guest cgroup's `memory.peak` during a job, and read pc1's `nproc` and `free -g`. Plan 4 vCPU and 6 to 8 GiB per guest; N is the smaller of (threads minus 2) over 4 and (RAM minus 4 GiB) over 9. pc1 still runs desktop services (KDE Connect and CUPS were named in the <issue id="c3a1a1b4-dad8-4263-87ed-18fd3ba8a7e5" href="https://linear.app/vaper/issue/GRS-57/move-clearcase-ci-to-a-disposable-vm-runner-on-pc1">GRS-57</issue> review), so it is not yet a dedicated host; decide whether to strip those first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pc1-vm create --instance 2` brings up a second guest and registers a second runner while instance 1 keeps running a job.
- [ ] Two CI jobs run at the same time on two guests, both PASS, with receipts.
- [ ] `scripts/ci/vm-boundary-probe` passes on both guests; neither can reach pc1's loopback, the other guest, multicast or broadcast.
- [ ] `pc1-vm destroy --instance 2` removes only instance 2's unit, directory, nft table and runner.
- [ ] `docs/ci-runner.md` documents instances, sizing numbers measured, and the host services decision.

## Reserved write scope

* scripts/ci/vm-host.sh
* scripts/ci/pc1-vm
* scripts/ci/guest-provision.sh
* docs/ci-runner.md

## Boundaries

Runner stops and host changes need the user's consent in a quiet window. No repository settings changes. One fresh independent diff review, one bounded fix round, fresh re-check. Only the coordinator changes Linear.

controls: **Roles.** First implementation runs on `claude-opus-5-5` at effort xhigh, independent diff reviews at xhigh and the recheck of a fix diff at high. Fixes from written findings, merges, and PR and Linear text run on `claude-sonnet-5-5` at high. A high finding that survives the fix round gets one Opus xhigh round with `diagnosing-bugs`. No agent runs at effort `max`. Deterministic checks run as scripts that leave receipts, not as model calls.

**Rare escalation.** Only a documented blocker that survives the normal loop escalates, to one of `claude-fable-5-1` at effort xhigh or `gpt-6-astra` at reasoningEffort xhigh, never both. Before dispatch, create the linked Linear escalation issue with the source issue, exact SHA, reproduction, prior attempts, bounded question, model, spend target and completion predicate. Afterwards, record the T3 task ID, findings, outcome, SHA and checks on it.

**Attempts.** One written-finding fix round with a fresh recheck, at most one justified rare escalation and one transient infrastructure retry. Stop when the same failure repeats twice without a new diagnosis. Attempts count against the original issue and stage, so renaming, restarting or redispatching a task does not reset them.

**Runtime.** Writing tasks get 90 minutes and reviews 30 minutes. Assess a stall after 30 minutes without meaningful progress. Declare bounded long tests and per-task deadlines in the brief, give a short checkpoint grace, cancel explicitly and keep the branch, evidence and cancellation result. A T3 wait timeout is not a runtime limit.

**Spend.** The targets are build 20, review 6, written fix 8, recheck 2 and escalation 12 USD. Report actual or unknown spend and the variance. Overspend alone does not pause, cancel or escalate work.
**Capacity.** At most three worker jobs and two browser jobs. PC2 is the first isolated synthetic test pool and PC1 keeps its CI role.

**Checks.** Scale checks to the change. App changes keep the required gate until its hosted replacement is reviewed, and documentation or research gets proportionate checks. Mutation and perf runs are for milestone gates only. A skipped, mocked, weakened or other-revision check is not a pass.

**Merge.** One branch and worktree per writing ticket, cut from the wave branch `wave/<name>` its brief names (or from the upstream ticket's branch while that is unmerged). A ticket PR targets its wave branch and a wave PR targets `dev`; nothing else targets `dev`. Merge commits only and serial integration on accepted upstream heads. The external reviewer `dianbrown` reviews the wave PR, and nothing merges into `dev` before that approval. `main` changes only through the user.

**Gate.** GRS-69 stays open until the user approves the complete written plan. No hosted work is dispatched before then, and every hosted runtime, provider and acceptance check is UNRUN. The hosted gate (GRS-138) is the required check for hosted tickets once it lands.

**Waves and checkpoints.** A wave is the set of tickets under one checkpoint aggregate (GRS-27, GRS-36, GRS-137, GRS-66, GRS-32), at most seven tickets, on one branch. At a checkpoint the user reads the aggregate report and drives the verification skill once. Agents run unattended between checkpoints. See [verification and review](plan/verification-and-review.md).

**Human gate.** Running the manual processing recipe over case documents is the user's own step in a separate chat. A worker stops with `AWAITING MANUAL RESULTS`, names the submission manifest and the download path, and resumes from the import step once the user supplies the package.
